main_body: Steampunk lamp post: a domed cap with an amber crystal on top, a lantern box with glowing amber windows, a thin pole with a collar, and a domed base
top_band: Cap at the top, x=8: rows 1-4 light grey L=148, then rows 5-7 mid grey L=122 (step of only about 26 L). At x=11 rows 1-7 are all L=122 with no step. This is dome shading, not a distinct top face.
evidence: The lantern and the pole are drawn as flat vertical faces seen straight on. The pole is a thin 2px shaft with no top surface. The upper cap and the base are domed shapes shaded left to right in the same grey family, so they read as dome silhouettes rather than a clear lighter top ellipse over a front face. The scan has no distinct front-edge line and no eave shadow, and at x=11 there is no light top band at all. The base has a light row at x=8 (row 36) and at x=4 (rows 37-39), but these are inconsistent across columns and only form a thin highlight. The result is a front elevation with dome silhouettes, not a clear 3/4 top plus front face.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 13 distinct colours against 38-40 for the references, and a median of 13 colours per tile against 17-20. Its grey ramp has about 5 steps plus an amber window, but there is almost no texture, grain or per-element highlighting. Dark edge pixels are 45% neutral, so the outline is partly near-black blue-grey rather than a consistent tinted material tone. The 13% flat-fill coverage is the same as the cheese stall, but the large dome areas are smooth gradients without dots or grain. Next to the stall and the well it looks thinner and more sticker-like.
